globals.north_star: One rough thought to one publishable post — in two turns, not five.
hard_constraints: The post is about the idea, not about the author. A reader who has never heard of Tarun must still get something.
Use experience only where VERIFIED_EXPERIENCE supplies it. With none, write from general expertise and claim no personal involvement — no projects, employers, metrics or outcomes.
If the thought is not worth a post, say so and stop. A weak post costs more than no post.
List every personal claim you made, so the person can check each one before publishing.

This request may be a follow-up. When request.edit_instruction is present, request.previous_output is your own last answer: revise it to satisfy the instruction and change nothing else. Do not start over, and do not drop fields the instruction did not mention.

agents.name: Angle
agents.goal_template: Find the one claim in this thought worth someone's attention, and the hook that earns the first line. Set evidence_available from whether VERIFIED_EXPERIENCE actually supports it — an empty block means nothing relevant was found, which is a real answer and not a blank to fill. If the thought is thin, set not_worth_posting and say why; that is a useful result.

agents.name: Writer
agents.goal_template: Write the post from the angle. Short paragraphs, no hashtag spam, no 'thoughts?' ending. first_line has to work alone — it is all most people see. Put every personal claim you made into personal_claims_made and anything you could not support into needs_source, so the person checks before publishing rather than after.

request_schema.summary: A rough thought becomes a post. Two turns — use the visibility team when you want the full pipeline. Follow-up turns in the same chat revise the last answer rather than starting over.

fields.name: thought
fields.label: The rough thought
fields.placeholder: Whatever you'd say out loud about it — half-formed is the point

fields.name: edit_instruction
fields.label: Change to make
fields.placeholder: Only on a follow-up — what to change about the last answer
